proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the effective lag is near-zero or varies over time, a fixed 1-week delay can shift peaks and degrade timing; may underfit multi-peak shoulders if dynamics are more complex than SEIR.
proposals.rationale: Primary low-complexity choice for a high-peakiness hospitalization-rate series where admissions plausibly lag an infectious proxy by ~1 week; avoids explicit H compartment to reduce identifiability risk on 31 training weeks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions systematically lag infections, this can produce forecasts that peak too early and misrepresent rise/decline slopes.
proposals.rationale: No-lag baseline to test whether the hospitalization-rate target aligns closely with the infectious proxy without an explicit reporting/admission delay; keeps parameterization minimal and stable.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Waning/reinfection may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season window, leading to spurious oscillation or over-flexible tails if waning is effectively too fast.
proposals.rationale: Adds minimal reinfection/waning channel while keeping observation as short-lag infectious proxy; intended to behave close to SEIR (slow waning) but can absorb mild late-season persistence without adding H dynamics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can confound lag effects with waning effects; may overfit late-season levels and reduce stability across rolling splits if reinfection is not supported by the data.
proposals.rationale: SEIRS variant to check whether any apparent persistence is better captured via slow waning rather than an observation lag; still avoids hospitalization compartment complexity.
